issues: Nothing to veto. The only change is DEPTH going from 8 to 6. It does not touch how val_bpb is measured, the data, the seed lines, the evaluation call or the prepare.py import.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. With a fixed 300 s budget, a shallower model runs more steps in the same time, so a lower val_bpb is plausible. A smaller model also uses less VRAM and does not add any code.

I couldn't recompute z exactly because the incumbent's standard deviation (or the exact z formula) isn't given. Candidate mean is 1.0853 and the incumbent mean is 1.1145, so the difference is 0.0292. The reported z = 7.118 matches an incumbent std of about 0.0041, which is consistent with the numbers given.

Only 2 candidate runs, and they differ by 0.005. That spread is larger than the implied incumbent std of about 0.004, so the estimate of the candidate's run-to-run noise is weak. Still, both runs are well below the incumbent mean, so accepting is reasonable.
